Regular Council Meeting CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
JOINT
REGULAR
MEETING
WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 9, 2008
6:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S. HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 at least 48 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24.
A full City Council agenda packet with all backup information is available at City Hall and the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library the Friday before each Council meeting and online www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents regarding an agenda item that are received after the distribution of the agenda and before 4:30 p.m. on the meeting day will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

2.
Employee Recognition of Retiring City Engineer Chandra Collure
Mayor Kellejian presented an award to Chandra Collure, City Engineer, for his past service of 14 years to the City and his retirement.
David Ott, City Manager, presented a gift to Chandra and thanked him for this service.
Chandra Collure, retiring City Engineer/Director of Public Works, said that his experience at the City had been positive. He introduced his daugher and son. He recounted some history of his employment with the City and thanked Council, staff and residents.
Sean McLeod addressed Chandra and thanked the City for employing him over the years and spoke to his working relations.
Paul Thompkins, former Mayor, stated that he helped the City with many accomplishments including his contribution on the Fiesta del Sol and help with setting up the new City Hall.
Dr. Ed Seigel honored Chandra’s work.
Chandra Collure’s son said that he was proud of his father and said that if he did half of what he does at home, he knows that he was appreciated.
Councilmember Nichols said that Chandra was very professional and had enjoyed working with him.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:
This portion of the agenda provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the City Council on items relating to City business and not appearing on today's agenda by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk. Comments relating to items on this evening's agenda are taken at the time the items are heard. Pursuant to the Brown Act, no action shall be taken by the City Council on public comment items. Items can be referred to the City Manager for placement on a future agenda. The maximum time allotted for each presentation is THREE MINUTES as per SBMC . (Be aware of the timer lights on the Council dais.)
Maureen Finkelstein said that she lives on S. Sierra, that there is a trailer park along Longs Drug Store where trailers appear to be unoccupied. She said that it affects her property value.
David Ott, City Manager, said that the City has addressed some issues over time and much of it is under the jurisdiction of the State of California and not the City. He said that some issues have been addressed and improved including concerns about safety and clean up.
Council and City Manager discussion ensued regarding that it is registered as a mobile home park with the state and until the current owner gets it de-certified other uses would not be possible, that there are some low income entitlements associated with the property that further complicate the matter, and that issues with the property are referred to the state and that the City has contacted the state on issues regarding utility lines falling down.
Marilyn Kalabsa asked council to consider allowed dogs to be off-leash during the off season. She said that she is a member of COOSA and they have decided to support the idea.

Item 16 Report (click here)
Item 16 documents distributed after the agenda posting
Lisa Foster, Interim City Attorney, responded to the letter submitted to Council on the item stating that it is an innovative ordinance, however Solana Beach was a unique city, and that the ordinance would not be on the agenda if the legality was in question. She said that the letter made two points regarding whether the City had sufficient justification and whether the City would enact on the taking of property if unable to develop property. She responded that the main justification for the ordinance was to protect and enhance visitor accomodation facilities, which is highly protected under state law and the Coastal Act to ensure coastal access as opposed to private owenrship and to provide low cost accomodations. She said that these types of ownership limit public access because they give exclusive rights and therefore limit access and tend to be expensive since they are typically luxury resorts and not affordable for the majority. She said that she disagreed with their conclusion of taking property and said that the standard for the taking of property is extremely high and she read languarge from the case that the letter cited pointing out the high standards that would be required. She concluded stating that the ordinance would hold up to state law.
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Campbell. Motion carried unanimously.
